safely check for pymc3 objects without dependency

Without introducing a fixed dependency on `pymc3`
(or any other non-standard library module),
this commit introduces facilities to safely
recognize `pymc3` objects (and objects with
origin in other modules).
This is achieved by reliance on standard
library module `importlib`.
In summary, we add a function with signature
`_has_type(object_, typename, module_path)`
that checks if `object_` has a type given as
string `typename` that can be found under a
`module_path`, also given as string.
If a module under `module_path` can not be imported
(e.g. because it is not installed), we returna `False`
`to cover cases where a user
does not use `pymc3`. We use this function to
refactor a few unsafe string-based checks
in `arviz.utils.utils`, for further information
on those check issue #138.

chg: removed leading underscore of `_autocorr`

Since `az.plots.autocorrplot` will use this
function from now on, it should no longer be
part of the "private" interface.

chg:autocorrplot <-`az.stats.diagnostics.autocorr`

Previously, values plotted in `az.plots.autocorrplot`
did not match values returned by
`az.stats.diagnostics.autocorr` exactly.
This commit introduces `az.stats.diagnostics.autocorr`
in `az.plots.autocorr`, unifying notions of
what `autocorrelation` is in `arviz` over both
interfaces.

removed `symmetric_plot`; fix y_lim to (-1, 1)

Symmetric plot is a rare usecase and supporting it
becomes more clumsy with our new interface
(we would have to essentially reverse append
autocorrelations to itself before plotting).
Limiting y axis bounds to (-1, 1) makes sense as
these are the natural bounds of the autocorrelation
values.

Several changes according to the PR discussion and other suggestions received.
* Functions _circular_mean() and normalize_angle() now are in numeric_utils.py.
* If the array has more than 1 dimension, _check_type() tries to flatten it silenty. If it is not possible, an error is raised.
* Improved how bw_fct type and value are checked and reported.
* All functions now start with _ because they are all internals.
* _select_bw_method() no longer exists. Its functionality is now incorporated into _get_bw().
* Changed internal _bw_* functions to a common signature.
* Added DeprecationWarning to _fast_kde() and now it calls _kde().
* Added tests for _normalize_angle() and _circular_mean().
The following functions and their backends have been modified to incorporate the circular argument that is passed to _kde() as well as the new meaning of the argument bw (see below):
* plot_density()
* plot_kde()
* plot_dist()
* plot_posterior()
* plot_violion()
* calculate_point_estimate()
In addition, plot_kde() gained a new argument, adaptive, which is used to determine if the bandwidth is adaptive or not.
Finally, note the meaning of the argument bw has changed. It used to be a bandwidth multiplication factor Now it can be either a string indicating the bandwidth method or the bandwidth itself. The internal function _kde() has an argument bw_fct which is the multiplicative factor.

Add new KDE function. (#1284)

* New KDE function.
Added a new KDE function that can be used to estimate linear and circular data.
Decided to put everything in a new file (instead of numeric_utils) because these functions
required many utilities themselves.
Also, updated all functions that used the old  function.
The circular option is not yet passed to higher level functions. That is something to be done.

* Update according to requests

* Fix how circular data is handled and listed changes in CHANGELOG.
* In the previous version the function  tried to normalize
the angles to [-pi, pi) but it was not correct.
This commit includes a function  that works appropiately.

* Update according to required changes.

* Several changes according to the PR discussion and other suggestions received.
* Functions _circular_mean() and normalize_angle() now are in numeric_utils.py.
* If the array has more than 1 dimension, _check_type() tries to flatten it silenty. If it is not possible, an error is raised.
* Improved how bw_fct type and value are checked and reported.
* All functions now start with _ because they are all internals.
* _select_bw_method() no longer exists. Its functionality is now incorporated into _get_bw().
* Changed internal _bw_* functions to a common signature.
* Added DeprecationWarning to _fast_kde() and now it calls _kde().
* Added tests for _normalize_angle() and _circular_mean().
The following functions and their backends have been modified to incorporate the circular argument that is passed to _kde() as well as the new meaning of the argument bw (see below):
* plot_density()
* plot_kde()
* plot_dist()
* plot_posterior()
* plot_violion()
* calculate_point_estimate()
In addition, plot_kde() gained a new argument, adaptive, which is used to determine if the bandwidth is adaptive or not.
Finally, note the meaning of the argument bw has changed. It used to be a bandwidth multiplication factor Now it can be either a string indicating the bandwidth method or the bandwidth itself. The internal function _kde() has an argument bw_fct which is the multiplicative factor.

* DeprecationWarning replaced by FutureWarning

* custom_lims in _kde() can be a tuple but then it tried to modify an inmutable object. Now it is converted to a list internally.
* test_kde_scipy() had a slicing step that was not necessary an caused an error when unpacking
* No error is raised when the data passed has lenght of 0 or 1. It raises a warning and returns np.nan

Use a generator to get bytes of `pydicom.Dataset`s

in `store_instances` of `DICOMwebClient`.

The `store_instances` method accepts a set of DICOM frames, dumps
them to bytes, and, finally, encodes them into a multipart/related
request.

The above process results in storing the original DICOM frames in
memory 3 times:

1. as the original `pydicom.Dataset` instances passed
   into `store_instances`
2. as bytes encoded in `store_instances`
3. as the concatenation of the above bytes created in
   `_encode_multipart_message`

Using a generator in `store_instances` reduces memory footprint by
1/3, since the original `pydicom.Dataset`s are dumped into bytes
one by one while the multipart request body is being created by
`_encode_multipart_message`.

I took that from https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet/blob/ecb6d79/dist/leaflet.css and added it where it would've been had it not been deleted out of Leaflet's CSS file, i.e. between "visual tweaks" and "popup". major overhaul (yes, again) of the ode package. Now much more simple, with single base class for residual and jacobian. Basically the idea is that we should create a policy only once, and be able to use it for any stepper method. The stpper knows to advance one step, the policy for the residual (or jacobian) knows what to do and how to evaluate the SPACE residual. For example, if one has to project the space residual, then this is only needed to be known to the policy. The stepper practically sees as if there was a residual computed, but it does not matter how it is computed as long as it mactches some requireents. If we need to leftmultiple the space residual (like in ROM we do), then you can envision this *modified residual* as the actual residual that is used by the stepper.

cleaning up and streamlining even more the policy folder. Rather than having a standard residual and jacobian for each of the methods, we now have a single standard residual and a single jacobian standard policy. Because before we were just having a lot of code duplication for no reason. Much cleaner now. Hopefully design works when we will implment roms. Need to test tomorrow

Adding a hacked version (for now) of QR factorization for epetra multivector wrapper.
This is needed becayse for LSPG we almost always have something like:

Let:
phi = basis,
y = reduced state
q = phi*y,  be the FOM state

time residual for backward Euler reduced form:
R(phi*y) = phi*y_n - phi*y_n-1 -dt f(phi*y_n,t_n) :

Jac(phi*y) = dR/dy = dR/dq * dq/dy => dR/dq * phi
dRdq = I - dt JJ(q,t_n)  where JJ is the application jacobian

when doing LSPG, we minimize R so we use QR factorization to factorize:
dR/dq*phi  = QU   (here U is the r factor)

Since typically the JJ is a sparse matrix, while phi is a multivector,
then for epetra/tpetra JJ*phi = multivector.
This is why we added/hacked for now a QR factorization for multivector

in a single way and deletage implementations.
